A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sampling-strategy study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references throughout. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original convergence and runtime experiments on Gaussian and ShapeNet data, plus dimensionality-reduction and clustering results on persistence diagrams and MNIST.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original empirical experiments and reports additional sampler comparisons, including Spherical Sliced Wasserstein results.

M1.justification: The work remains a comparison of existing sampling algorithms. V3 introduces Bonet et al.'s Spherical Sliced Wasserstein sampler as another surveyed comparator, without proposing a new estimator or adaptation. The retained algorithms are not reformulated; the Riesz step-size revision concerns experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gaussian data in dimensions 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, and 50; twelve persistence-diagram ensembles; the same three ShapeNet objects; and MNIST in 784 dimensions. The distance-approximation and dimensionality-reduction tasks are retained.

E2.justification: V3 adds SSW comparisons on Gaussian, ShapeNet, and MNIST data. Gaussian comparisons add normalized Sobol variants in dimensions 5, 10, and 20, and randomized normalized Halton enters the higher-dimensional timing plots. Conversely, MNIST drops randomized Halton, Sobol, and randomized Sobol rows.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported Riesz gradient step from 0.1 to 1, retaining ten iterations and s=0.1. The added SSW evaluation specifies 250 iterations, learning rate 150, and 500 great circles. Dataset construction, projection-count grids, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The exact two-Dirac ground-truth sanity check is retained from v1 Remark 4 to v3 Remark 9. No new ablation or robustness test appears. The added Riesz scalability discussion extrapolates existing timing and complexity information rather than reporting a new experiment.

E5.justification: MNIST results retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. Neither version supplies experimental seed or repeated-run counts, and v3 adds no confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure. Revised uncertainty values accompany changed results, not a changed reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 4.1, 4.2, and 4.5 gain sampler results, and the MNIST table adds SSW while removing three comparator rows. Under the unchanged stated MNIST design, Halton's reported MDS NMI/ARI change from 0.56/0.08 to 0.91/0.75 without explanation (v1 Table 4; v3 Table 5). Persistence-diagram scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 adds a general-measure Lipschitz statement and proof argument under finite second moments, retaining the discrete regularity argument separately. It withdraws v1 Proposition 3's universal orthonormal variance-reduction inequality and instead establishes unbiasedness while disclaiming that inequality. New Section 3.3 also introduces the SSW definition, metric conditions, and complexity analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal user-guide contribution remain stable. Section 5 withdraws the claimed theoretical guarantee for orthonormal sampling and the specific recommendation to precompute Riesz points for large projection counts. It also adds broader efficiency claims, including that i.i.d. sampling is slowest in all experiments.

C2.justification: V3 explains orthonormal sampling's empirical benefit through sample diversity, expands the explanation of high-dimensional LDS limitations, and restricts the amortization argument for Riesz generation to moderate sample counts. It removes the conclusion's explicit high-dimensional SHCV implementation caveat and identifies a Sobol implementation limit above dimension 20.

D1.justification: V3 supplies the SSW implementation reference, initialization, and optimizer settings; credits the Riesz implementation source and identifies riesz_noblur.py; and adds explicit SciPy references and the Sobol implementation restriction. The main repository address is retained.

R1.justification: Related-method coverage expands through Bonet et al. (2023) on SSW and supporting spherical-projection and metric references, including Quellmalz et al. (2023) and Liu et al. (2024). Sphere mappings gain additional sources. The comparative user-guide positioning and principal earlier sampling literature remain intact.

P1.justification: V3 numbers previously unnumbered subheadings, inserts the SSW subsection, and rewrites the orthonormal discussion and parts of the conclusion. Citation formatting and terminology receive local edits, while the main section order and most prose remain stable. An unresolved citation and stray new markers appear in v3.

P2.justification: V3 adds the convergence/time/space-complexity summary in Table 2 and a dimensions column to the acronym table. Existing comparison plots gain curves and revised colors, legends, and axis ranges; taxonomy and MNIST table rows also change. The original figure types, panel arrangements, and single-column format are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the guide more useful by withdrawing the general orthonormal variance-reduction guarantee, adding SSW comparisons and a complexity summary, and qualifying Riesz scalability. These gains are tempered by unexplained MNIST revisions and comparator removals, plus an overbroad timing claim: Figure 4.2f shows SSW taking longer than i.i.d. sampling at comparable errors.
